content.user_title: Manage Git Worktrees for Parallel Development
content.value_statement: Parallel branch work can become slow when one checkout blocks another task. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Git worktree workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Git worktrees fit parallel feature, hotfix, and PR review workflows.
Shows how to create worktrees for existing branches and new branches.
Lists worktrees and describes clean, dirty, detached, and prunable states.
Guides cleanup of merged worktrees with a visible dry-run style plan.
Provides configuration guidance for a shared worktree base directory.
limitations: It does not include executable scripts or automated validation.
It relies on Git being installed and available to the assistant.
It cannot guarantee that cleanup commands preserve uncommitted work.
It assumes users approve paths and branches before commands run.

use_cases.title: Work on Two Features
use_cases.description: Create a separate checkout for a second branch while preserving current edits in the original directory.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request Safely
use_cases.description: Open a review branch in an isolated worktree so tests and inspection do not disrupt active work.

use_cases.title: Clean Finished Worktrees
use_cases.description: Identify merged worktrees, preview cleanup actions, and remove stale directories after user confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: List Current Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my current Git worktrees and summarize the branch, commit, and working state for each one.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Feature Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a worktree for a feature branch while keeping my current branch untouched.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through reviewing a pull request in a separate worktree without disturbing my current changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my worktrees, identify merged branches, and propose a cleanup plan that asks before removing anything.

output_examples.output: The assistant returns a concise inventory with each worktree path, branch, commit, status, and cleanup notes.

output_examples.input: I need a hotfix without touching my current work.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes an isolated hotfix worktree, names the branch, explains the location, and lists next steps.
The assistant lists merged candidates, separates risky entries with uncommitted work, and asks for confirmation before removal.

best_practices: Confirm the target branch and worktree path before creating or removing anything.
Check for uncommitted changes before cleanup or force removal.
Keep worktrees in a predictable directory outside the main repository.
anti_patterns: Do not remove worktrees before checking for uncommitted changes.
Do not place linked worktrees inside the main repository tree.
Do not reuse one branch in multiple active worktrees.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps an assistant plan and explain Git worktree creation, listing, review workflows, hotfix isolation, and cleanup.

faq.question: Does it run Git commands by itself?
faq.answer: The skill provides guidance for assistants with Bash access, but users should approve destructive commands.

faq.question: Can it protect uncommitted changes?
faq.answer: It reminds the assistant to check status and warn about dirty worktrees before cleanup.

faq.question: Does it support new branch creation?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes creating a new branch and linked worktree in one workflow.

faq.question: Can it help with pull request review?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines an isolated worktree flow for reviewing a pull request without changing current work.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
